reason: The book is up +1.77% net of the mega-cap tech GARP core plus the SOXL short hedge, and the tape confirms the thesis rather than breaking it, so a trade into a live FOMC event would just add churn cost for no edge. CME FedWatch-style pricing shows ~90% odds of a hold at 3.75-4.00% for the 2026-09-16 decision versus ~10% for a 25bp cut, so tomorrow's outcome is already the consensus case and not a surprise the book needs to pre-position around. AVGO's -6.36% leg looks like sentiment noise, not thesis failure: it trades at $344 against a Street 'Strong Buy' consensus and a $533 target (~55% upside), and management reiterated AI revenue guidance on the last call -- exactly the kind of quality-name dip a GARP book should sit through rather than sell into. The SOXL short is doing its job (+14.64% on the leg) as chip stocks are described in the press as having 'turned into the market's pain trade' on AI-capex-pace worries, which is the froth this leg was built to hedge, so cutting it now would remove protection right before a rate event that could reignite that rotation. UNH (-4.48%) got one sell-side downgrade on slow multi-year growth but also a constructive Optum/WellMed stake sale to TPG and expanded prior-auth relief -- a mixed, not broken, picture that argues for staying put rather than realizing the drawdown. META/GOOGL/MSFT are all green and IWM/COST/XOM are roughly in line with thesis. With cash already at 20% as dry powder and 20bps+ of round-trip cost to replace the book, the highest-value action into a well-priced, high-probability-hold FOMC is to hold and let the event resolve before making any capital-allocation change.
